decisions.rationale: Mimikyu and Palafin as the lead pair provide immediate offensive pressure: Mimikyu can Swords Dance into Play Rough to delete Fairy leads like Floette-Eternal and threaten Hatterene, while Palafin's Aqua Jet priority and Flip Turn pivot enable the Hero-form sweep that is the core win condition. Aegislash and Toxapex on the back bench cover the defensive needs — Aegislash walls physical attackers with King's Shield and checks Psychic/Fairy types, Toxapex absorbs Garchomp's Earthquakes and provides Haze as a safety net. Glimmora and Skarmory (bench 5-6) enter later to stack hazards once safe, supporting the Palafin sweep plan.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leans hyper-offensive with Mega Floette, Garchomp, Scrafty, and Trick Room Hatterene. Our win condition is Palafin Flip Turn into Hero-form sweep after Glimmora/Skarmory hazards stack. Mimikyu SD Play Rough deletes key Fairy/Psychic threats. Aegislash King's Shield cripples physical attackers. Toxapex Regenerator + Haze handles Garchomp and resets field. Priority backbone: Aqua Jet, Shadow Sneak (Mimikyu/Aegislash), Tailwind from Skarmory lets the whole team outrun 150 Spe.

decisions.rationale: Lead Talonflame and Garchomp for immediate Gale Wings Tailwind pressure and strong spread damage into likely Skarmory/Glimmora leads. Milotic provides the safest Palafin answer and speed control backup, while Mega Floette is retained as a fast late-game cleaner once Steel-types are weakened.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster is Mimikyu, Palafin, Aegislash, Toxapex, Glimmora, Skarmory. Prioritize preserving Milotic for Palafin and avoid exposing Mega Floette to healthy Aegislash or Skarmory. Talonflame Sash and Gale Wings Tailwind are key tools for controlling the fast mode; Garchomp Rock Slide pressures the opponent's Flying/Rock options and Earthquake requires ally positioning care.

decisions.rationale: Palafin's Aqua Jet at +1 priority outspeeds and hits Talonflame super-effectively before it can Tailwind or Taunt, applying crucial early pressure on the fastest foe. Mimikyu uses Swords Dance to set up its sweep potential; Disguise negates the first incoming hit (e.g., Garchomp's Earthquake), letting Mimikyu safely boost and threaten Fairy/Psychic targets next turn.

decisions.rationale: Priority Taunt denies Mimikyu’s Swords Dance while Protect shields Garchomp from the immediate Fairy/Ice pressure, preserving the stronger midgame board against Palafin.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed sets: Mimikyu is Focus Sash Adamant with Swords Dance; Palafin is Life Orb Adamant with Zero to Hero and Flip Turn. Preserve Milotic for Palafin, and avoid exposing Mega Floette to healthy Aegislash or Skarmory. Talonflame’s Sash/Gale Wings remains a key speed-control resource.

decisions.rationale: Mimikyu is under volatile Taunt but can still use attacking moves; Play Rough into Garchomp exploits the super-effective Fairy coverage and Garchomp's reduced-accuracy Protect from last turn. Palafin uses priority Aqua Jet into Talonflame to finish off the 43% HP Fire/Flying threat with a guaranteed super-effective hit before Talonflame can Tailwind or attack.

decisions.rationale: Double-switching preserves both threatened attackers while placing Water-resistant Milotic into Talonflame’s slot and Fairy-type Floette into Garchomp’s slot, making the most likely Water and Fairy attacks unfavorable.

Mimikyu Play Rough guarantees a KO on 36% Floette-Eternal (37-73% damage range eliminates all legal defense spreads), removing the Energy Ball threat that could OHKO Palafin. Palafin Flip Turn on Milotic deals damage, switches Palafin out to activate Zero-to-Hero form on reentry, and avoids leaving Palafin in against Floette-Eternal's super-effective Energy Ball. Speed order: Palafin (120) acts first with Flip Turn (+1 priority), then Floette-Eternal's retargeted move hits Palafin's substitute (Toxapex/Aegislash) at neutral damage, then Mimikyu (116) cleans with Play Rough.

decisions.rationale: Mimikyu-Busted can only pass or forfeit; passing preserves board presence with its boosted Attack and Play Rough coverage while Milotic acts first. Switching Palafin's fainted slot to Toxapex brings in a Water-type pivot that resists Milotic's Muddy Water, threatens Garchomp with neutral Ground coverage while taking reduced Earthquake, provides Regenerator longevity, and carries Haze to reset Milotic's Competitive boosts and any future setup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent hyper-offensive core: Mega Floette fainted, Garchomp/Talonflame remain. Win condition: Palafin Hero-form sweep once threats are managed. Toxapex's Haze and Regenerator make it the ideal pivot against Garchomp and stat-boosting opponents. Mimikyu Disguise already broken; retain as offensive check. Floettite and Leftovers confirmed items.

decisions.rationale: Mega Floette gets its strongest available Palafin pressure before Mimikyu can remove it, while Icy Wind breaks Disguise and gives enduring Speed control over both foes for the remaining endgame.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette has Fairy Aura and reaches 169 Speed with this Timid build. Palafin’s priority Aqua Jet can act before faster attacks; Mimikyu’s Focus Sash and Disguise must be accounted for. Preserve Milotic as the primary Palafin answer when feasible; Talonflame remains valuable for speed control.

decisions.rationale: Bring Talonflame to preserve Garchomp and establish Tailwind pressure while Milotic remains healthy against the unrevealed backline.
decisions.notebook: Talonflame is the key speed-control option; preserve Milotic for Water threats and Garchomp for late-game physical pressure when possible.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Talonflame (43% HP, FocusSash broken) to eliminate the Gale Wings priority threat before it can fire off a devastating Brave Bird or Flare Blitz. Toxapex's Liquidation is super effective (2x) against Talonflame, and Mimikyu's Shadow Claw hits neutrally. Removing Talonflame's Gale Wings priority is the most urgent defensive play, after which Aegislash can pivot in to safely bring Palafin for the Hero-form sweep.
decisions.notebook: Opponent hyper-offensive core: Garchomp and Talonflame remain. Win condition: Palafin Hero-form sweep once priority and physical threats are managed. Need to eliminate Talonflame Gale Wings priority before pivoting to Aegislash for Palafin setup.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Double-target Mimikyu before it can set up or pressure Garchomp; Talonflame moves first and Milotic follows before either foe, giving the best immediate chance to remove it while Talonflame is likely lost to Toxapex afterward.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mimikyu is Adamant Focus Sash with Play Rough, Shadow Claw, Swords Dance, Shadow Ball; Toxapex is Regenerator Shell Bell with Toxic, Recover, Haze, Liquidation. Prioritize removing Mimikyu before exposing Garchomp to Play Rough; preserve Milotic for Water matchups and use Talonflame as speed-control or tempo when viable.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

King's Shield (priority +4) protects Aegislash from Garchomp's Earthquake and drops Garchomp's Attack by 2 stages, dramatically reducing the super-effective spread damage Toxapex would also take. Toxapex's Liquidation (100% accuracy, neutral 1x damage) reliably chips Garchomp while Shell Bell provides passive recovery. This combination mitigates the biggest immediate threat (Garchomp's Earthquake) while maintaining offensive pressure, setting up a favorable position to eventually pivot to Palafin once physical threats are managed.
Earthquake is the only strong simultaneous pressure into both foes; Recover restores Milotic after the allied spread damage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mimikyu is Adamant Focus Sash with Play Rough, Shadow Claw, Swords Dance, Shadow Ball; Toxapex is Bold Regenerator Shell Bell with Toxic, Recover, Haze, Liquidation. Aegislash is Careful Leftovers with King's Shield, Shadow Sneak, Flash Cannon, Sacred Sword. Prioritize removing Mimikyu before exposing Garchomp to Play Rough; preserve Milotic for Water matchups and use Talonflame as speed-control or tempo when viable.

decisions.rationale: Aegislash uses King's Shield (priority +4) to block Garchomp's expected Earthquake, which would KO Toxapex regardless. A successful shield leaves Aegislash at full HP with Garchomp's Attack crippled by -2, making Aegislash very difficult to break next turn. Even if the shield fails (reduced success rate), Aegislash may survive the combined Earthquake + Muddy Water damage. Toxapex at 12% HP is almost certainly KO'd by Garchomp's spread Earthquake before acting, so Toxic targeting Milotic is chosen as the highest-value contingency — poisoning Milotic cripples the opponent's primary recovery and special attacker if Toxapex somehow survives or if the opponent's plan changes.
decisions.notebook: Opponent hyper-offensive core: Garchomp and Talonflame remain. Win condition: Palafin Hero-form sweep once priority and physical threats are managed. Floettite and Leftovers confirmed. Mimikyu Disguise broken. Toxapex is the ideal Regenerator pivot against Garchomp. Need to eliminate Talonflame Gale Wings priority before pivoting to Aegislash for Palafin setup. Garchomp has Def -1 from Toxapex Liquidation. If King's Shield lands, Garchomp Attack drops further to -3, making Earthquake negligible and enabling Aegislash to 2HKO with Flash Cannon next turn.

decisions.rationale: Protect Garchomp from Liquidation and safely let Milotic’s faster Muddy Water remove the critically low Toxapex before it can Recover; this preserves Garchomp to pressure Aegislash afterward.
decisions.notebook: Against Aegislash plus a low-HP Toxapex, prioritize a protected Milotic spread attack to deny Toxapex recovery while preserving Garchomp for Ground pressure.

decisions.rationale: Aegislash uses King's Shield to block Garchomp's incoming attack and drop its Attack to -3, neutralizing Earthquake and setting up a Flash Cannon KO next turn. Toxapex at 1% uses Recover to attempt to survive the turn as a Regenerator pivot, since foes act first and any other action wastes its remaining HP without saving it.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake guarantees Toxapex is removed even if Muddy Water misses, while Muddy Water adds pressure into Aegislash; Milotic survives the allied spread damage.
decisions.notebook: When facing Aegislash alongside a critically low Toxapex, use Garchomp Earthquake to ensure Toxapex cannot Recover, accepting manageable allied spread damage; pair it with Milotic Muddy Water for additional Aegislash pressure.

decisions.rationale: King's Shield is the optimal move for Aegislash. It has priority +4 so it resolves first, protecting Aegislash from both Garchomp's Earthquake and Milotic's Muddy Water. Garchomp's Earthquake is a contact move, so King's Shield will drop Garchomp's Attack by 2 stages on top of the existing -1 from Liquidation, bringing it to -3. This effectively neuters Earthquake and sets up a Flash Cannon 2HKO next turn, which is the stated win condition. Toxapex has fainted so the only legal action is Pass.

Recover preserves Milotic through toxic and allied Earthquake while Garchomp applies the only meaningful immediate pressure to Aegislash; it also covers a successful King’s Shield without sacrificing Milotic.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Aegislash is Careful Leftovers with King's Shield, Shadow Sneak, Flash Cannon, and Sacred Sword. Its King’s Shield can fail on consecutive use, so maintain Earthquake pressure while preserving a partner to punish failed shields.

decisions.rationale: King's Shield is the critical play: it has priority +4 so it fires before Garchomp's Earthquake. If it lands, it blocks the super-effective Earthquake entirely and drops Garchomp's Attack by 2 stages (on top of the existing Def -1), crippling Garchomp's offensive threat and setting up a Flash Cannon KO next turn. Toxapex is fainted so the only legal action is Pass.

Earthquake has the immediate super-effective KO line if King's Shield fails; Recover gives Milotic the best chance to survive Garchomp's spread damage and remain useful if Shield succeeds.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp's Earthquake at 2x super-effectiveness guarantees a KO on Aegislash at 31% HP (60.6–87.1% damage). Any move other than King's Shield results in Aegislash fainting. King's Shield (priority +4) blocks the incoming Earthquake, drops Garchomp's Attack by 2 stages (neutering its primary weapon for the Palafin sweep), and leaves Aegislash alive to act next turn. Milotic's follow-up hit (Muddy Water ~14–21% or Icy Wind ~2.6–4.5%) is survivable. Toxapex is fainted so only Pass is available.

Floettite and Leftovers confirmed. Mimikyu Disguise broken. Toxapex is the ideal Regenerator pivot against Garchomp. Milotic is badly poisoned at 28% and will be a secondary target after Garchomp's Attack is neutered.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake guarantees the KO if Aegislash’s reduced-success King’s Shield fails; Recover is the only available partner action with any potential value.

King's Shield is the only play that can negate Garchomp's super-effective Earthquake while also dropping its Attack by 2 stages. Even with the reduced Protect success rate, the upside—surviving this turn and making Garchomp's Earthquake trivial next turn—is far better than any attacking move, which would let Earthquake hit unopposed and likely OHKO Aegislash at 37%. Toxapex is fainted so Pass is forced.
decisions.notebook: Opponent hyper-offensive core: Garchomp remains as the sole active threat. Floette-Mega and Talonflame are fainted. Milotic fainted and tox. Win condition hinges on Aegislash surviving to neuter Garchomp's Attack via King's Shield, then cleaning with Sacred Sword/Flash Cannon. Floettite and Leftovers confirmed on opposing fainted Pokémon. Mimikyu Disguise broken. Toxapex Regenerator pivot role fulfilled. Palafin Hero-form sweep deferred—Palafin is fainted and cannot be revived this game.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake is a guaranteed KO if King's Shield fails; its repeated use has sharply reduced success.
decisions.notebook: Aegislash is Careful Leftovers with King's Shield, Shadow Sneak, Flash Cannon, and Sacred Sword. Repeated King's Shield attempts have sharply reduced success; maintain Ground pressure against it when shield odds are low.

reflections.summary: Aegislash ran out of King's Shield PP (all 8 uses exhausted by Turn 12), leaving it unable to block Garchomp's super-effective Earthquake and resulting in a fatal OHKO. The team preview also proved suboptimal—Palafin and Talonflame were both eliminated early by the opponent's Mega Floette and Garchomp pressure, forcing Aegislash into a frontline role from Turn 4 onward and accelerating its PP drain.
reflections.adjustment: Slot Aegislash into the starting four instead of one of the early-game fainted Pokémon (e.g., replace Talonflame) so King's Shield PP is preserved from the outset against Garchomp. This gives Aegislash more staying power to neuter Garchomp's Attack and survive to clean.
reflections.notebook: Opponent hyper-offensive core confirmed: Garchomp is the primary win condition and will spam Earthquake to break King's Shield PP. Floette-Mega is a mid-game nuke—took out Palafin before falling to a crit; respect its Fairy Aura-boosted Moonblast. Milotic is a bulky pivot (Leftovers, Recover, Haze, Toxic); Toxic support from Toxapex is effective against it. Aegislash King's Shield has 8 PP—must not be front-loaded against Garchomp without backup. Hatterene (Trick Room, Psychic, Magic Bounce) and Scrafty (Intimidate, FakeOut) are untapped reserves—potential surprise picks next game. Floettite confirmed on Floette; Leftovers confirmed on Milotic. Next game: start Aegislash to conserve King's Shield PP; consider bringing a secondary Garchomp check or Rocky Helmet chip to punish contact.

reflections.summary: Won by neutralizing Mimikyu with Talonflame's Taunt, trading efficiently through Palafin, then using Mega Floette/Milotic pressure to establish Garchomp as the endgame win condition. The four brought suited the matchup, and Mega Floette was the correct evolution for immediate Fairy Aura-boosted Palafin pressure, though its early critical-hit KO reduced its value. Piloting was clean; Garchomp correctly kept attacking once Aegislash's repeated King's Shield attempts became unreliable.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, preserve Mega Floette more carefully after it removes or heavily damages Palafin—use Protect or position Talonflame/Garchomp to deter Mimikyu's Play Rough rather than accepting a direct follow-up. This retains stronger endgame coverage against the opponent's Dark-/Dragon-vulnerable targets and reduces reliance on a low-HP Garchomp cleanup.
reflections.notebook: Opponent brought Mimikyu, Palafin, Aegislash, and Toxapex in game 1; Glimmora and Skarmory were not brought. Mimikyu is Adamant Focus Sash with Play Rough, Shadow Claw, Swords Dance, and Shadow Ball; it can be shut down early by Taunt. Palafin is Adamant Life Orb with Aqua Jet, Wave Crash, Ice Punch, and Flip Turn; prioritize Fairy/Grass pressure and respect priority Aqua Jet. Toxapex is Bold Shell Bell Regenerator with Liquidation, Toxic, Recover, and Haze; it can poison bulky waters and sustain, so use strong Ground pressure. Aegislash is Careful Leftovers with King's Shield, Shadow Sneak, Flash Cannon, and Sacred Sword. It repeatedly used King's Shield; continue Ground pressure and attack when consecutive Shield odds fall. Game-1 plan that worked: Talonflame + Garchomp lead, bring Milotic and Mega Floette; Mega Floette is a strong Palafin answer, but preserve it from Mimikyu when possible.
